request.spec:
The sheet has an alert threshold (settings, two decimals, blank means off, not dated;
SETTING_CHANGED key=alert-threshold value=<amount>). After a change's rollup lines, for each person
whose due-total went from at or below the threshold (or no due-total) to above it, one line ALERT
name=<name> due-total=<due-total> is written, in list order. A person already above it writes no
further ALERT until their due-total has been at or below the threshold and crosses it again. An
ALERT line, like ROLLUP and TOTALS, never ends with for=.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has an alert threshold (settings, two decimals, blank means off, not dated;
SETTING_CHANGED key=alert-threshold value=<amount>). After a change's rollup lines, for each person
whose due-total went from at or below the threshold (or no due-total) to above it, one line ALERT
name=<name> due-total=<due-total> is written, in list order. A person already above it writes no
further ALERT until their due-total has been at or below the threshold and crosses it again. An
ALERT line, like ROLLUP and TOTALS, never ends with for=.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The alert threshold is in, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What I changed:**
- **The setting** (`Setting.java`, `ValidateSetting.java`): a new `alert-threshold` setting. It is not dated, takes an amount with up to two decimals, and blank means off. Any other value is refused with an error. It is saved and logged through the existing settings route, so it writes `SETTING_CHANGED ... key=alert-threshold value=<amount>`.
- **The screen** (`access.slot.tsx`): an "Alert threshold" field in the Settings panel. Its placeholder says "off".
- **The ALERT lines** (`Rollup.java`): after a change's ROLLUP and TOTALS lines, if a threshold is set, one `ALERT name=<name> due-total=<due-total>` line is written for each person who crossed it, in list order. Crossing means their due-total was at or below the threshold (or they had none) before the change and is above it after. ALERT lines never end with `for=`; the audit service already treated them that way.

**One choice you may want to check:** the app keeps no per-person "already alerted" record. Each change compares the person's due-total just before it with just after it, using the threshold set now. That covers every case the test checks, including someone who drops below, comes back above and alerts again.

The difference shows when the threshold itself changes. Say someone is at 3.00 when the threshold goes from 5.00 down to 1.00. Changing the setting writes no ALERT, and their next rise doesn't either, because they were already above the new threshold before it. They only alert after dropping to or below 1.00 and rising again. If they should instead alert the first time a change finds them above a threshold they've never been alerted for, that needs a stored flag per person.
